$comment: Holdout expectations, derived by hand from the doctrine's engine descriptions AFTER ruleDigest (sha256 of the concatenated rule surface named by RULE_SOURCES in packages/ds-codegen/src/analytical/necessity.ts) was recorded, and never tuned to the engine's output. Each expectation is a judgment in canonical tuple form: [code|term, subject, assertion, engine, evidenceClass]. If engines.ts changes, the digest check fails; the remedy is to re-derive every expectation by hand and re-record, not to copy the engine's output. Re-record log: 27701a78... (authored) -> 5fc0509d... after REL-UNIT-DIAGNOSTIC-CAUSE-RENAME-01 (identifier rename; no expectation changed) -> 493d9bd2... after REL-FIELD-ALGEBRA-02 Phase A (occurrence identity gained the assertion key and the emitting engine; the suppression obligation moved to declaration-missing; subjects lost the '#kind:op' suffix). Every item re-derived by hand in the new form; no code, subject locus, or evidence class changed. -> 6b7b2135... after REL-FIELD-ALGEBRA-02 Phase B (the kernel: capabilities replace scale labels, rollup is an aggregate, max is min's alias, target grain gone). Every item re-derived by hand against the kernel engine description; only two occurrence KEYS changed, both in FX_H_KPI_INDEX_AND_RATE (aggregate:max -> aggregate:min; rollup:sum(toGrain=quarter) -> aggregate:sum); no code, subject, engine, or evidence class changed. -> c2141c64... -> 9cb24f4e... -> 03db3460... -> 19853c84... across REL-VIEW-ALGEBRA-01. Four moves, one argument. The slice added the derivation boundary and wired it into judge() (c2141c64), then made the boundary three-valued and ran it BEFORE assertion evaluation so an unadmitted result cannot lend standing to assertions over it (9cb24f4e), then widened the digest's domain from engines.ts alone to the whole rule surface in RULE_SOURCES order, engines.ts then derivation.ts (03db3460) — because a digest over one module would let a rule move into the other and change freely while this file still claimed to be current — and finally replaced two literal NUL separator bytes in derivation.ts with spaces (19853c84), which git had been reading as a binary file and therefore refusing to diff. What discharges the re-derivation duty here is a REACH argument, not eight independent re-derivations: no fixture in fixtures.jsonl declares a derivedBy, so checkDerivations returns empty for every holdout item, the ungrounded set is empty, no assertion is withheld, and the boundary cannot reach any of these eight judgments. That argument was then checked mechanically — all eight items still match their recorded expectations exactly and all eight report zero derivation occurrences (tmp/reverify-holdout.mts). The expectations themselves were not touched, and no status, code, subject, assertion key, engine or evidence class changed. Note what this does NOT cover: because no fixture yet exercises a derivation, the boundary's own rules are pinned only by unit tests, and the first fixture that declares a derivedBy will need its expectation derived by hand, not read off the engine.
